e-8383.worked_solution:
The definition of $\cosh{x}$ is

$$
\cosh{x} = \dfrac{1}{2}(e^{x} + e^{-x}).
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cosh}⁡(\operatorname{ln}⁡2) & =\frac{1}{2}({e}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}+{e}^{-\operatorname{ln}⁡2}) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}({e}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}+{e}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡{2}^{-1}}) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(2+{2}^{-1}) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(2+\frac{1}{2}) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(\frac{4+1}{2}) \\  & =\frac{5}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\sinh{x} = \dfrac{1}{2}(e^{x} - e^{-x}).
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sinh}⁡1 & =\frac{1}{2}({e}^{1}-{e}^{-1}) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(e-\frac{1}{e}) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(\frac{{e}^{2}-1}{e}) \\  & =\frac{{e}^{2}-1}{2e}.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{tanh}⁡x & =\frac{{e}^{x}-{e}^{-x}}{{e}^{x}+{e}^{-x}} \\  & =\frac{{e}^{2x}-1}{{e}^{2x}+1} \\  & =\frac{1-{e}^{-2x}}{1+{e}^{-2x}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the second definition, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{tanh}⁡4 & =\frac{{e}^{2(4)}-1}{{e}^{2(4)}+1} \\  & =\frac{{e}^{8}-1}{{e}^{8}+1}.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 6
?

Given that y≥0, which of the following is equivalent to sinh⁡y?

a
12(ey−e−y)
b
12(ey+e−y)
c
12(e−y−ey)
d
2(ey−e−y)
e
2(ey+e−y)
Submit

decision.explanation: By definition, sinh(x)=(e^x-e^{-x})/2. Substituting x=√y gives option a.

t6+12t3

t3−1t3
d
t3+1t3
e
t6−12t3

The definition of sinh⁡x is

sinh⁡x=12(ex−e−x).

Therefore, sinh⁡(ln⁡t3)=12(eln⁡(t3)−e−ln⁡(t3))=12(eln⁡(t3)−eln⁡((t3)−1))=12(eln⁡(t3)−eln⁡(t−3))=12(t3−t−3)=12(t6−1t3)=t6−12t3.

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{tanh}⁡x & =\frac{{e}^{x}-{e}^{-x}}{{e}^{x}+{e}^{-x}} \\  & =\frac{{e}^{2x}-1}{{e}^{2x}+1} \\  & =\frac{1-{e}^{-2x}}{1+{e}^{-2x}}.\end{aligned}

$$
